schemes.name: PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)
schemes.description: Central Sector scheme, 100% funded by the Government of India, operational from 1 December 2018. It gives direct income support to landholding farmer families to help meet agricultural input and domestic expenses.
schemes.eligibility_summary: Landholding farmer families whose names appear in the state/UT land records. Families are identified and verified by the State/UT government. Certain higher-income exclusion categories (institutional landholders, serving/retired government employees above the notified thresholds, income-tax payers, and notified professionals) are not eligible.
schemes.benefits: INR 6,000 per year, paid in three equal installments of INR 2,000 each for April-July, August-November and December-March, transferred directly to the bank account through Direct Benefit Transfer.
schemes.application_instructions: Register on the official PM-KISAN portal or through the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC). The State/UT government verifies your land record and exclusion status before the benefit is released.
schemes.source: PM-KISAN Operational Guidelines and PIB press releases, Government of India

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
schemes.description: Comprehensive crop insurance covering pre-sowing to post-harvest losses caused by natural calamities such as drought, flood, hailstorm, unseasonal rain, pests and disease.
schemes.eligibility_summary: Farmers growing notified crops in notified areas for the applicable season. Cover is offered season by season and enrolment windows are set by the state.
schemes.benefits: Sum insured is paid for notified crop loss. The farmer pays only a capped premium: 2% of sum insured for Kharif foodgrain and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi foodgrain and oilseed crops, and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops, or the actuarial rate, whichever is less. The balance premium is subsidised, shared 50:50 between the Centre and the State (90:10 in the North Eastern Region).
schemes.application_instructions: Apply through the official PMFBY portal, a bank branch, an insurance agent or a Common Service Centre before the notified cut-off date for the season.
schemes.source: PMFBY Operational Guidelines and PIB, Government of India

schemes.name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) with Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS)
schemes.description: KCC gives farmers a single composite credit facility for crop production and allied activities including animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries and bee-keeping. MISS makes the short-term loan cheaper.
schemes.eligibility_summary: Owners, tenants, oral lessees, sharecroppers, cultivators and eligible self-help groups / joint liability groups. Each land parcel is covered through one KCC account. Final sanction rests with the lending bank.
schemes.benefits: Short-term crop loans are lent to farmers at 7% per annum. An additional 3% prompt-repayment incentive is given to farmers who repay on time, so the effective rate is 4% per annum. As per the RBI notification for FY 2025-26 the interest subvention applies on an overall limit of INR 3 lakh; loan limits and collateral-free limits have been enhanced in recent announcements, so confirm the current limit with your bank.
documents: Land records or proof of cultivation rights
schemes.application_instructions: Apply at any commercial bank, regional rural bank, cooperative bank or PACS branch. Farmers can also approach a bank camp organised under the nationwide KCC saturation drive.
schemes.source: Reserve Bank of India notification on Modified Interest Subvention Scheme for FY 2025-26, and PIB press notes

schemes.name: Soil Health Card Scheme
schemes.description: Government scheme that tests your soil and issues a Soil Health Card giving the nutrient status of the land together with recommended dosages of fertiliser, bio-fertiliser, organic manure and soil amendments.
schemes.eligibility_summary: Soil samples are collected and tested by the State Agricultural Department for farmers in the notified area. Contact your block or village agriculture assistant to be included in a sampling cycle.
schemes.benefits: A free soil test and a printed or digital Soil Health Card in 22 languages with nutrient status and crop-wise nutrient dosage recommendations, supporting need-based input use, lower cultivation cost and sustainable soil health.
schemes.application_instructions: Apply through the Soil Health Card portal or ask your village agriculture assistant / Krishi Vigyan Kendra to collect a soil sample from your field.
schemes.source: Soil Health Card portal, Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

schemes.name: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)
schemes.description: A pan-India electronic trading portal that networks existing APMC mandis into a single national market. Implemented by the Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC) under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.
schemes.eligibility_summary: Farmers selling notified commodities at an e-NAM integrated mandi. Participation requires the mandi to be part of the e-NAM network and the trader to hold the applicable unified licence.
schemes.benefits: Transparent auction-based price discovery with real-time demand and supply, access to buyers beyond the local mandi including other states, online bidding, and timely payment into the farmer's bank account.
documents: Farmer registration on the e-NAM portal
schemes.application_instructions: Register on the e-NAM portal, bring your produce to an e-NAM integrated mandi, and take part in the physical plus online auction. Toll free helpdesk: 1800 270 0224.
schemes.source: e-NAM official portal, Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare
